title: Unit 1 Mixed Review Review Test
description: Reinforce the essential Unit 1 geometry relationships with direct and moderate practice.

questions.questionText: Point (2, -3) is translated 4 units left and 6 units up. What is the image?
questions.explanation: Subtract 4 from x and add 6 to y.

questions.questionText: Point (-5, 2) is reflected across the y-axis. What is the image?
questions.explanation: Reflecting across the y-axis changes the sign of x.

questions.questionText: Point (3, 4) is rotated 180 degrees about the origin. What is the image?
questions.explanation: A 180 degree rotation sends (x, y) to (-x, -y).

questions.questionText: Which transformation is rigid?
questions.explanation: A translation preserves lengths and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles 36 degrees and 84 degrees. What is the third angle?
Remote interior angles are 44 degrees and 59 degrees. What is the exterior angle?
Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are what?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when the lines are parallel.

questions.questionText: Two figures are congruent. What must be true?
options: They have the same size and shape.
questions.correctAnswer: They have the same size and shape.
questions.explanation: Congruent figures match in size and shape.

questions.questionText: Point (-2, 6) is reflected across the x-axis, then translated 3 units right. What is the final image?
questions.explanation: Reflect to (-2, -6), then translate right to (1, -6).

questions.questionText: Two same-side interior angles are 110 degrees and x degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles add to 180 degrees.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles x degrees, 2x degrees, and 90 degrees. What is x?
An exterior angle is 124 degrees. One remote interior angle is 52 degrees. What is the other remote interior angle?
Point (4, -1) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What is the image?
questions.explanation: A 90 degree counterclockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (-y, x).

questions.questionText: A figure is translated and reflected. What is preserved?
questions.explanation: Translations and reflections are rigid transformations, so side lengths are preserved.

questions.questionText: Two alternate interior angles are 4x + 3 degrees and 2x + 41 degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: 4x + 3 = 2x + 41, so x = 19.

questions.questionText: A triangle has exterior angle 132 degrees. Its remote interior angles are equal. What is each remote angle?
questions.explanation: The equal remote angles share 132 degrees.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles in the ratio 1:2:3. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: There are 6 parts, so each part is 30 degrees and the largest angle is 90 degrees.

questions.questionText: Which evidence proves two grid figures are congruent?
options: A sequence of translations, reflections, and rotations maps one onto the other.
One figure has larger side lengths.
One figure is a dilation of the other by 2.
The figures have the same color.
questions.correctAnswer: A sequence of translations, reflections, and rotations maps one onto the other.
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is evidence of congruence.

questions.questionText: A point (x, y) is reflected across the y-axis. What is the rule?
questions.explanation: A y-axis reflection changes x and keeps y.

questions.questionText: A right triangle has one acute angle of 37 degrees. What is the other acute angle?
questions.explanation: The two acute angles in a right triangle add to 90 degrees.
